title: NFOs and offer documents: SID, SAI and KIM
objectives: Explain what each offer document contains.
body_md:
## Documents

| Document | Content |
|---|---|
| **SID** (Scheme Information Document) | Scheme-specific: objective, asset allocation, risks, costs, loads |
| **SAI** (Statement of Additional Information) | Fund-wide: constitution, AMC, trustees, legal |
| **KIM** (Key Information Memorandum) | Summary of the SID and SAI; given with the application form |
| **Addendum** | Notifies changes during the life of the scheme |

## NFO basics

- A **New Fund Offer** raises money for a new scheme at a face value of **₹10** per unit (typical).
- The NFO must be open for no more than **15 days**.
- Units are allotted within **five working days** of closing.
- An NFO is **not cheaper** because the price is ₹10; the NAV only starts there.
- Many categories already exist; an NFO should fill a real need, not just follow a trend.

## Advertising rules

Ads must be **fair, not misleading** and carry the standard risk statement: *Mutual fund investments are subject to market risks, read all scheme related documents carefully.*

> **Exam tip:** SID is scheme-specific, SAI is fund-wide, KIM is the summary.
example: A client says an NFO at ₹10 is cheaper than a ₹150 NAV fund. A ₹10 NAV simply means fewer rupees per unit; it does not mean better value.
say: The KIM comes with the form; please read the SID for the scheme's risks and costs.
An NFO at ₹10 is not a bargain; compare it with existing funds.
never: Buy the NFO, it is only ₹10 per unit.
No need to read the documents.

check.q: The document with scheme-specific details is the:
The maximum period an NFO can stay open is:
check.why: An NFO can be open for at most 15 days.

check.q: A ₹10 NAV compared with ₹150 NAV means the NFO is:
o: Not necessarily cheaper; unit price only
check.why: Unit price does not show value.
